name: Elm
summary: The language The Elm Architecture comes from, and the reference every other entry is graded against.
notes: Only elm/* packages may define effect managers, so a new kind of Cmd or Sub (websockets, a new browser API) goes through ports.
Frameworks written in Elm (elm-pages, elm-land) are libraries of this column, not entries of their own.

name: Gren
summary: A fork of Elm with its own package set, which also runs on Node for command line tools and servers.
notes: update returns { model, command } with command a Cmd msg the runtime runs, and Browser.element takes subscriptions : model -> Sub msg (https://github.com/gren-lang/browser/blob/main/src/Browser.gren).
Programs on Node use the same Model, update and subscriptions without a view: Node.defineProgram takes init, update and subscriptions (https://github.com/gren-lang/node/blob/main/src/Node.gren).

Ports are typed: a port module declares port toJs : String -> Cmd msg and port fromJs : (String -> msg) -> Sub msg, and compiler 0.6.0 added task ports (https://gren-lang.org/book/applications/ports/).

name: Lamdera
summary: Elm on both sides: a second TEA loop runs on the server, with typed messages between frontend and backend.
notes: Superset: server-side TEA. The backend has its own Model, update and subscriptions (Lamdera.backend takes init, update, updateFromFrontend and subscriptions); data sync and migrations are part of the platform.

Lamdera.frontend is Browser.application plus updateFromBackend; sendToBackend, sendToFrontend and broadcast are Cmd values, and Lamdera.onConnect is a Sub (https://github.com/lamdera/example-apps/tree/master/counter/src).
Ports work on the frontend only (the elm-pkg-js folder is injected by the compiler); the backend has no ports or JavaScript (https://dashboard.lamdera.app/shouldnt-use).

name: Miso
summary: A Haskell front-end framework with the Elm shape, plus components, server-side rendering and hydration.
notes: Superset: components with their own model, update, view and subscriptions (since 1.9), and server-side rendering with hydration.
Subscriptions are user-defined: createSub acquires and releases their resources when a component mounts and unmounts.
update schedules effects with io; it does not run them.

name: Monomer
summary: A native desktop GUI toolkit for Haskell, inspired by Elm.
notes: handleEvent returns [AppEventResponse s e]: Model replaces the model, Event raises another event, and Task (one IO result) and Producer (many events) are effects handed to the runtime (https://github.com/fjvallarino/monomer/blob/main/src/Monomer/Widgets/Composite.hs).

No subscriptions function: a Producer is started by returning it from handleEvent (for example on AppInit), and the runtime keeps its async thread and feeds its events back (docs/tutorials/05-producers.md).

Composite widgets nest a child with its own handleEvent and buildUI over a lens into the model of the parent (composite takes an ALens into it, Monomer.Widgets.Composite), the nested pattern of Elm, so the entry is full TEA.

name: gi-gtk-declarative
summary: Declarative GTK for Haskell; its app-simple package runs an Elm-style loop.
notes: update : state -> event -> Transition state event, and Transition state (IO (Maybe event)) returns the IO action as a value that the runtime runs and feeds back (gi-gtk-declarative-app-simple, GI.Gtk.Declarative.App.Simple).

No subscriptions function: App has a fixed inputs :: [Producer event IO ()] list, run by the loop for its whole life and cancelled when it ends; GTK signals are routed to events by the library (subscribe, cancel).
The core gi-gtk-declarative package is only the declarative widget layer; the Elm-style loop lives in the app-simple package.

name: Flame
summary: A fast and simple PureScript framework inspired by The Elm Architecture.
notes: Superset: server-side rendering with Flame.Renderer.String.render and hydration with resumeMount, which takes over a page rendered on the server and restores its serialized model (https://github.com/easafe/purescript-flame/blob/master/docs/rendering.md).

update returns Tuple Model (Array (Aff (Maybe Message))); the effects are Aff values the runtime runs, and each one may raise another message (https://github.com/easafe/purescript-flame/blob/master/docs/events.md). noMessages is the shorthand for no effects.

No subscriptions function: subscribe is a fixed Array (Subscription Message) given at mount (Flame.Subscription.Window, Document and onCustomEvent), and Flame.Subscription.send raises a message from anywhere.
Interop with JavaScript goes through CustomEvent subscriptions: onCustomEvent prime decodes a JSON payload (UnserializeState) into a message.
Mostly maintained by one developer.

name: Elmish (PureScript)
summary: The Elm Architecture in PureScript, rendering through React.
notes: Superset: wrapWithLocalState turns a component into a React component with its own message, update and transition loop, independent of its parent, which keeps its state (https://github.com/collegevine/purescript-elmish/blob/master/docs/composition.md).

update returns Transition msg state, a state plus an Array of Command values (Elmish.Component.transition, fork); the runtime runs them in Aff after update returns and dispatches the messages they produce (https://github.com/collegevine/purescript-elmish/blob/master/docs/transition.md).
No subscriptions function: Elmish.Subscription.subscribe starts a Subscription from a Transition, usually init, and the runtime stops it when the component unmounts.
No ports: JavaScript is reached through the React FFI (ReactComponent, Elmish.Foreign) from inside effects, since it is a thin layer on top of React.
Maintained by CollegeVine and used in production there.

name: Pux
summary: An early Elm-style framework for PureScript, kept for its history.
notes: Superset: isomorphic rendering, with renderToString and waitState to render on the server once data has loaded (https://github.com/alexmingoia/purescript-pux/blob/master/docs/rendering.md).
foldp :: Event -> State -> EffModel State Event returns { state, effects :: Array (Aff (Maybe Event)) }; the effects are Aff values that start runs and whose events are fed back to foldp.
No subscriptions function: inputs is a fixed Array (Signal Event) given to start (for example the URL signal for routing), and app.input is a channel to send events from anywhere.
The last commit to master is from 2018 and it is built on purescript-signal and smolder.
Ports are managed: start returns the app with input, a Channel that it creates, so outside code can send events into the running app (src/Pux.purs).

name: Spork
summary: Elm-like apps in PureScript on a fast virtual DOM, close to Elm in speed.
notes: update returns Transition effects model action, a record { model, effects :: Batch effects action }; the effects are data (a functor you choose) that an Interpreter runs and turns back into actions (src/Spork/Transition.purs, src/Spork/Interpreter.purs).
subs :: model -> Batch subs action is a function of the model that picks the active subscriptions, and the runtime starts and stops them as the set changes (src/Spork/App.purs).
PureApp is the simple form with update :: Model -> Action -> Model and no effects or subscriptions; BasicApp has effects but no subs.
Ports are managed: the AppInstance that App.make and makeWithSelector return has push, which buffers an action from outside for the next tick (src/Spork/App.purs).

name: Elmish (Fable)
summary: The Elm Architecture for F#, compiled to JavaScript by Fable; the base of a large family of F# frameworks.
notes: update is 'msg -> 'model -> 'model * Cmd<'msg>; Cmd<'msg> is a list of effects (Dispatch<'msg> -> unit) that the runtime runs (Cmd.OfAsync.perform, Cmd.OfPromise.either, Cmd.ofEffect).

Program.withSubscription takes 'model -> Sub<'msg>, a list of (SubId, Dispatch -> IDisposable); the runtime diffs it after each update, starting new ids and disposing removed ones (since v4; the timer sample in docs/docs/subscription.fsx uses it).
No ports: JavaScript is reached with Fable imports from inside effects and subscriptions, and the program gives the host no handle to send messages in.

view is 'model -> Dispatch<'msg> -> 'view and the runtime is renderer-agnostic: Bolero, Elmish.WPF, Avalonia.FuncUI, ReactiveElmish.Avalonia and Xelmish run on the Elmish package for WebAssembly, desktop and games.

name: Bolero
summary: Elmish on Blazor: F# web apps in WebAssembly.
notes: Superset: server-side rendering through Blazor render modes (BoleroRenderMode Server, WebAssembly, Auto, with prerender) and stream rendering (Program.mkStreamRendering loads the model after the first render).

Runs the standard Elmish 4 loop in ProgramComponent: update returns Model * Cmd<Msg> (Elmish.Cmd.OfAsync.perform), and Program.withSubscription subscriptions are started in OnAfterRenderAsync (ProgramRun.fs).

Ports are managed: ProgramComponent has a public Dispatch, the dispatch method of the component, so Blazor code holding it can send messages in (src/Bolero/Components.fs); JavaScript is also reached through the effect types Cmd.OfJS and Cmd.OfAuthorized.
ElmishComponent only re-renders when its sub-model changes; it has no model of its own.

name: Elmish.WPF
summary: Elmish for Windows desktop apps, with the view in WPF XAML bound to the model.
notes: WpfProgram.mkProgram takes init and update returning 'model * Cmd<'msg> (Elmish.Cmd), and mkProgramWithCmdMsg lets update return plain command data that a toCmd function turns into Cmd.
WpfProgram.withSubscription takes 'model -> Sub<'msg> and passes it to Elmish 4, whose keyed subscriptions are started and stopped automatically (src/Elmish.WPF/WpfProgram.fs).

The view is a list of bindings (Binding.oneWay (fun m -> m.Count), Binding.cmd Increment) over static XAML, a function of the model but not one that returns a view tree; graded the same as ReactiveElmish.Avalonia.

name: Fabulous
summary: Declarative native mobile and desktop apps in F#, on .NET MAUI and Avalonia.
notes: Superset: components that own local state and can embed an independent MVU program (Context.Mvu), beside the root program.

Program.statefulWithCmd takes init and update returning 'model * Cmd<'msg>; Cmd is a list of effects run by the runtime (Cmd.OfAsync.perform, Cmd.OfTask.either), and statefulWithCmdMsg lets update return command data mapped by mapCmd.
Program.withSubscription takes 'model -> Sub<'msg>, a list of (SubId, Dispatch -> IDisposable) that the runtime starts and stops by id as the model changes (Sub.fs).
view is 'model -> WidgetBuilder<'msg, 'marker>, reconciled with the native UI of MAUI or Avalonia; there are no ports, the host is .NET.

name: Avalonia.FuncUI
summary: Cross-platform desktop apps in F# on Avalonia, with an Elmish integration and its own component model.
notes: Superset: Component (fun ctx -> ...) with hooks (ctx.useState, useEffect) gives nested stateful components with local state, beside the Elmish integration.

TEA comes from Avalonia.FuncUI.Elmish over Elmish 5: Program.withHost and Program.runWithAvaloniaSyncDispatch run a standard Elmish program, so update returns Model * Cmd and Program.withSubscription takes a keyed function of the model (ClockApp example); ctx.useElmish runs the same loop inside one component.
The README Elmish counter shows an update that returns only the state; the loop itself is the Elmish runtime, so Cmd and Sub work as in Elmish.
view is 'state -> dispatch -> IView, a tree of component descriptions that the host diffs; there are no ports.

name: Terminal.Gui.Elmish
summary: Elmish over Terminal.Gui, with a view DSL in the style of Feliz.
notes: update is 'msg -> 'model -> 'model * Cmd<'msg>; Cmd<'msg> is a list of Sub (Dispatch -> unit) effects that the runtime runs (Cmd.ofSub, Cmd.OfAsync.perform, Cmd.ofMsg).

Sub is managed: the package carries its own copy of the Elmish 3 loop, so Program.withSubscription takes 'model -> Cmd<'msg>, runs once at start and is never restarted or stopped; a source that lives on is a Cmd that dispatches again (the Spinned message in the counter, timerSubscription in App.fs).
view is 'model -> Dispatch<'msg> -> TerminalElement built with the Feliz-style View.label and View.button DSL; the runtime diffs the tree (TreeDiff.fs). There are no ports.
A port to Terminal.Gui v2 is published as OnurGumus.Terminal.Gui.Elmish.

name: bucklescript-tea
summary: A close port of the Elm API to OCaml and ReScript, continued as rescript-tea.
notes: The program record is init: flags -> model * msg Tea_cmd.t, update: model -> msg -> model * msg Tea_cmd.t (model first, not second as in Elm), view: model -> msg Vdom.t and subscriptions: model -> msg Tea_sub.t (src-ocaml/tea_app.ml).

Cmd and Sub are values the runtime runs: Tea.Cmd.batch, Tea.Cmd.msg, Tea.Task.perform, and Tea.Sub.registration, whose enable and disable calls run when a subscription appears in or leaves the result of subscriptions (Tea.Time.every is built on it).
No typed ports: JavaScript can push messages into a running program through the programInterface (pushMsg), and Tea.Cmd.call runs a callback; other interop is direct BuckleScript externals.
The last commit is from November 2023; the README points to the philip2 tool for porting between Elm and OCaml, and darklang/rescript-tea is a ReScript fork.

name: ocaml-vdom
summary: Elm-style virtual DOM apps in OCaml through js_of_ocaml, by LexiFi.
notes: An app is { init : model * msg Cmd.t; update : model -> msg -> model * msg Cmd.t; view : model -> msg vdom } (Vdom.app); Vdom.simple_app is the form with no commands.

Cmd is an extensible type: Vdom.Cmd has echo, batch, map and bind, and anything else (HTTP, timers) is a constructor you add and a Vdom_blit.Cmd.handler you register, which reports the outcome with Vdom_blit.Cmd.send_msg (see examples/demo/demo.ml).
There is no subscriptions function in the app record: a long-running source is a command handler that keeps calling send_msg, for example from a Window.set_timeout.

Ports are managed: Vdom_blit.process app msg sends a message into a running app from outside (lib/vdom_blit.mli); interop with JavaScript otherwise goes through command handlers and Vdom_blit.Custom controllers (custom elements), not typed ports.

name: Lustre
summary: The Elm Architecture in Gleam, in the browser and on the server, with universal components.
notes: Superset: server components run the update loop on the Erlang target and patch the DOM over a socket (since 5.5 they can join supervision trees), and components can be registered as custom elements.
There is no subscriptions function: long-running sources are effects that keep dispatching.

name: Shore
summary: A terminal UI framework for Gleam following The Elm Architecture, on the Erlang runtime.
notes: update returns #(Model, List(fn() -> Msg)); each fn is an effect the runtime spawns in an unlinked process and sends back to update as a message (task_handler in src/shore/internal.gleam).
There is no subscriptions function: a long-running source is an effect that returns a message and is scheduled again by update, or a process that sends to the Subject given by spec_with_subject.
start returns a Subject, so outside code can send messages into the program (spec_with_subject, shore.send).
Needs Erlang/OTP 28 or later (https://github.com/bgwdotdev/shore/blob/main/README.md).

name: Teashop
summary: A Gleam terminal framework inspired by Bubble Tea and Mint Tea.
notes: update returns #(Model, Command(Msg)); Command is a data type (set_timer, quit, execute_process, sequence, and command.from for a custom effect that gets a dispatch function) run by the JavaScript runtime.
There is no subscriptions function: a repeating source is command.set_timer rescheduled from update, or a command.from effect that keeps calling dispatch.
The messages of the app arrive wrapped in event.Custom(msg) next to event.Key and event.Resize; teashop.send(dispatch, msg) sends one from outside.
JavaScript target only; last commit February 2024.

name: gleamtea
summary: A terminal UI framework for Gleam on top of beamtea, a Bubble Tea for Erlang.
notes: update(msg, model) returns #(Model, Cmd(msg)); Cmd is a data type (Quit, Msg, Tick, Every, Task, Batch, Seq) run by the beamtea runtime (https://github.com/tsirysndr/gleamtea/blob/main/src/gleamtea.gleam).
There is no subscriptions function: Every(ms, msg) is a repeating timer the runtime runs until the program quits, and Task(fn) runs a function and delivers its result.
The messages of the app arrive wrapped in User(msg) next to Key and Resize.
Typed bindings to beamtea (https://github.com/tsirysndr/beamtea), which can be used from Erlang directly.

name: Ratatouille
summary: A declarative terminal UI kit for Elixir, built on The Elm Architecture.
notes: The app behaviour has init(context), update(model, msg) returning a model or {model, Command.t}, render(model) and an optional subscribe(model).
Effects are Ratatouille.Runtime.Command values: Command.new(fun, message) runs the function in a Task and the result comes back to update as {message, result}; Command.batch groups them.
subscribe returns Subscription.interval(ms, message) or Subscription.batch, but the runtime reads it once at startup, so the subscriptions are fixed for the life of the program.
The last commit is from October 2021.

name: Tyrian
summary: An Elm-inspired UI library for Scala 3 and Scala.js, by the makers of the Indigo game engine.
notes: update returns (Model, Cmd[F, Msg]); Cmd is data (Cmd.Run, Cmd.SideEffect, Cmd.Emit, Cmd.Batch) over a Cats Effect F that the runtime runs (https://github.com/PurpleKingdomGames/indigoengine/blob/main/tyrian-platform/src/tyrian/platform/Cmd.scala).

subscriptions(model): Sub[F, Msg] is a function of the model; Sub.make, Sub.fromEvent and Sub.fromStream carry an id and a release, and the runtime starts and stops them (https://github.com/PurpleKingdomGames/indigoengine/blob/main/tyrian-platform/src/tyrian/platform/Sub.scala).
No ports: interop goes through Sub.make, Sub.fromEvent, Cmd.Run and Scala.js facades, and TyrianApp.launch returns Unit, so the host has no handle to send messages in.
Began as a fork of Scalm; a bridge lets a Tyrian app and an Indigo game talk through their messages.
Moved in 2025 to the indigoengine monorepo with Indigo; the old repository is archived.

These grades are of the released API (TyrianIOApp, Cmd and Sub); the 0.30 milestones on main add tyrian.App, whose update returns a Result, with watchers and extensions (mini apps composed into their parent).

name: Indigo
summary: A functional game engine for Scala.js whose loop is a variation of The Elm Architecture.
notes: Superset: SubSystems are mini games with their own state, update and present, kept by the engine and talking to the game only through events (indigo/shared/subsystems/SubSystem.scala); scenes split a game the same way.
Frame driven: updateModel(context, model) returns GlobalEvent => Outcome[Model], and a FrameTick event arrives every frame; the view is present, which returns a SceneUpdateFragment.

Outcome carries the next model and the events to emit; the engine performs the effect events among them (PlaySound, AssetEvent.LoadAssets, ScreenCaptureEvent) and sends results back as events (AssetEvent.AssetBatchLoaded), a closed set as in Elm. Arbitrary I/O is meant to go through an embedding Tyrian app (https://github.com/PurpleKingdomGames/indigo-docs/blob/main/website/documentation/misc/indigo-vs-elm.md).
Messages are GlobalEvent, an extendable trait, so they are open as tea.Msg is in Bubble Tea.
No subscriptions function: input, frame and viewport events are built into the engine and arrive on their own, and a SubSystem is the sanctioned place for a long-running source such as the network.
Game.events.push sends events in and Game.events.eventCallback reads events out, from outside the game.
Moved in 2025 to the indigoengine monorepo with Tyrian; the old repository is archived.

name: Scalm
summary: Elm-inspired Scala.js library, the ancestor of Tyrian.
notes: update(msg, model) returns (Model, Cmd[Msg]) in the App trait (in the plain Scalm.start form update returns only a Model); a Cmd is Cmd.RunTask over a Task that the runtime executes (src/main/scala/scalm/Effects.scala).
subscriptions(model): Sub[Msg] is a function of the model; Sub.every, Sub.timeout and Sub.fromEvent carry an id and a cancel, and the runtime starts and stops them when the ids change.
No ports: host callbacks are wrapped as an Observable inside effects (Sub.ofTotalObservable, Task.RunObservable), and Scalm.start gives no handle to send messages in.
Scala 2.12 and Scala.js 0.6 only; last commit February 2018 (repository pushed to in 2021).

name: react-tea-cup
summary: The Elm Architecture for React and TypeScript, with tea-cup-fp for Cmd, Sub, Task and Port.
notes: ProgramWithNav turns URL changes into messages.
Renders in the terminal through Ink: the realworld example has a TUI admin built on it.
Component packages (forms, router, drawer, pagination) live in tea-cup-package.

name: Foldkit
summary: A TypeScript frontend framework built on Effect: one Model, one update, and side effects as values the runtime runs.
notes: Superset: server rendering with hydration is built in, and Mounts and ManagedResources manage element lifecycles and stateful handles; Submodel composes child models with OutMessages, as nested modules do in Elm.

update returns { model, commands? }; a Command is a named Effect value (Command.define) that the runtime forks and whose result comes back as a Message (https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit/blob/main/packages/foldkit/src/update/update.ts).
Subscription.make takes modelToDependencies and dependenciesToStream; the runtime diffs the dependencies after each Model change and restarts the Effect Stream only when they change.
Port.inbound and Port.outbound are Schema-typed channels to the host, reached through the EmbedHandle of Runtime.embed.
All in on Effect by design; purity inside update is kept by convention and an oxlint plugin, not by the compiler.

name: elm-ts
summary: A port of The Elm Architecture to TypeScript on fp-ts, RxJS and React.
notes: update returns [Model, Cmd<Msg>]; a Cmd is an Observable of fp-ts Tasks that the runtime runs (src/Cmd.ts).

program takes subscriptions: (model) => Sub<Msg>, and the runtime switchMaps over the model stream so subscriptions restart when the model changes (src/Platform.ts); Sub is an RxJS Observable (src/Time.ts every).
No ports (the README lists "no ports" among the differences from Elm), but program returns dispatch, so outside code can send messages in (src/Platform.ts).
tea-effect presents itself as its spiritual successor.

name: tea-effect
summary: The Elm Architecture on Effect, with React hooks; started in 2026 as a successor to elm-ts.
notes: Superset: the useProgram hook (React.makeUseProgram) runs a program inside a React component, so each feature mounted through it keeps its own loop and state in React.
update is (msg, model) => [Model, Cmd<Msg>]; a Cmd is an Effect Stream of messages that the runtime runs (src/Cmd.ts, src/Platform.ts).
Platform.program takes subscriptions: (model) => Sub<Msg>; subscriptions are keyed Effect Streams, and the runtime diffs the keys after each model change so only the delta starts or stops.
No ports: there is no Port module, but the program returns dispatch, so outside code can send messages in (src/Platform.ts).
Platform.program is a headless runtime.

name: @typescript-tea/core
summary: A framework-agnostic TEA core for TypeScript, with effects as data and the view left to React or another library.
notes: update returns readonly [State, Cmd<Action>?]; a Cmd is a plain value { home, type } that the runtime hands to the EffectManager matching its home (src/cmd.ts, src/program.ts).
Program has an optional subscriptions: (state) => Sub<Action>; after each update the runtime gathers the Subs and calls every EffectManager, which starts and stops its sources.

No ports: the host plugs in through an EffectManager of your own (setup, onEffects, onSelfAction), passed as the last argument of Program.run, in the way of the effect managers of Elm; run returns only a function that ends the program.
Msg is called Action and Model is called State; there is no built-in view library, and view is a pure function of state and dispatch that a library such as React renders.

name: react-elmish
summary: The Elmish pattern for React, with commands and subscriptions.
notes: Superset: each React component runs its own loop with its own model, messages and update (useElmish), whose state React keeps; the view is the component.
update returns [Model, Cmd?] (an UpdateMap or an update function); a Cmd is an array of functions of dispatch, and useElmish runs them with execCmd after the update (src/cmd.ts, src/useElmish.ts).

Sub is managed: the subscription function runs once on mount, returns functions of dispatch, and the destructor each one returns runs on unmount; it does not follow the model (https://github.com/atheck/react-elmish#subscriptions).
No ports: parent and host communication goes through callback props, called by a Cmd.

name: Hyperapp
summary: A tiny JavaScript framework whose actions return new state with effects, and whose subscriptions are a function of the state.
notes: Untyped: messages are action functions rather than a closed union; an action (State, Payload) -> [NextState, ...Effects] is the update step for its own message, and the docs call actions messages.
update returns the next state, or an array of the next state and effects; effects are [effecter, payload] values the runtime runs after the state change (docs/architecture/effects.md).
subscriptions: (state) => [...] is a function of the state; the runtime diffs the list after every state change and starts and stops each subscriber (patchSubs in index.js).
app() returns the dispatch function, which controls the app from outside; calling it with no arguments stops every subscription.

name: Ferp
summary: Elm-style state, effects and subscriptions for JavaScript, in the browser or in Node.
notes: Headless: no view; app takes init, subscribe and observe, and observe is a callback that sees each state so any presentation layer can render it.
Untyped: an action is a function (state) => [state, effect], as in Hyperapp; effects are values built by effects.none, batch, defer, thunk and act, which the runtime runs in effectStage.
subscribe(state) returns a list of sub(fn, ...params) values; subscribeStage diffs the list after every action by function and parameters, starts new ones and calls cancel on the removed ones.
app() returns dispatch, which feeds actions from outside.

name: iced
summary: A cross-platform, renderer-agnostic GUI library for Rust, inspired by Elm.
notes: update(&mut self, message) returns a Task<Message>, a set of actions the iced runtime runs; Task::perform turns a future into a message (runtime/src/task.rs).

subscription(&self) -> Subscription<Message> is a function of the state; Subscription::run and run_with start a stream that the runtime keeps alive while it stays in the returned value, and time::every is built on it (futures/src/subscription.rs).
No ports: there is no typed boundary to the host; a program calls Rust directly.
Not a superset: the stateful widget::Component, whose state the runtime keeps, is deprecated in the 0.14 release behind the lazy feature, and apps compose screens in the nested pattern of Elm.

name: libcosmic
summary: The toolkit of the COSMIC desktop, built on iced, with app, applet and theming layers on top.
notes: The loop is the one of iced: cosmic::Application has update(&mut self, message) -> Task<Self::Message> (a type alias of iced::Task) and subscription(&self) -> Subscription<Self::Message>, with Task::none and Subscription::none as defaults (src/app/mod.rs).
What libcosmic adds (widgets, theming, the shell of an app or a panel applet, optional D-Bus activation hooks such as dbus_activation) is a toolkit, not a part of the architecture, so it is full TEA.

name: Sauron
summary: A Rust web framework heavily inspired by Elm, with the view built from plain function calls.
notes: Superset: nested components with their own message type, update and view (Component, StatefulComponent, usable as custom elements; update returns Effects with follow-ups and messages for the parent), and server-side rendering with render_to_string (examples/ssr-forms).
Application::update(&mut self, msg) -> Cmd<Msg>; Cmd::once and Cmd::new take a future that resolves to a message, and the runtime polls it (crates/core/src/dom/cmd.rs).
No subscriptions function: a long-running source is a Cmd::recurring built over a channel, as Window::on_resize and Window::on_mousemove do, kept by the runtime.

Ports are managed: Program::mount_to_body returns the Program, whose dispatch sends a message from outside (crates/core/src/dom/program.rs); JS interop otherwise goes through wasm_bindgen and web_sys directly.

name: tears
summary: A TEA framework for terminal apps on ratatui, inspired by Elm, iced and Bubble Tea, with async commands.
notes: Superset: tears::testing::TestStore drives update and the effects of commands in virtual time and fails a test on any unchecked output, and reducers compose like TCA (scope, for_each over a Keyed collection, presented over an optional Slot) with the effects of a removed child torn down (https://github.com/akiomik/tears/blob/main/README.md).

update(&mut self, msg) returns a Command<Message> (none, perform, future, stream, batch, map, cancel, retry, timeout, quit); async work is a Command the runtime runs, and the result returns as a message.

subscriptions(&self) returns a Vec<Subscription<Message>> from the model; each has an identity from its source key, and the runtime reconciles after every update, starting new ones and stopping removed ones. Sources: Timer, TerminalEvents, Signal, and WebSocket and HTTP behind features.
view(&self, frame: &mut Frame) draws into a ratatui Frame.

name: hojicha
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal UIs in Rust on ratatui, inspired by Bubble Tea.
notes: update(&mut self, event: Event<Message>) returns a Cmd<Message>, a data type (NoOp, Function, Async, Tick, Every, Batch, Sequence, Quit, ExecProcess) that the runtime runs; view(&self) returns a String.

No subscription function: commands::every is a repeating timer Cmd, and Program::subscribe(stream) (also subscribe_interval) returns a Subscription handle that forwards stream items as messages until it is cancelled or dropped.
Ports are managed: Program has sender(), send_message(msg) and init_async_bridge(), which returns a SyncSender for messages from outside (hojicha-runtime src/program.rs).
GPL-3.0 licensed.

Its repository (https://jgok76.gitea.cloud/femtomc/hojicha) redirects to a sign-in page, so the site links the docs; the source was read from the published crates hojicha-core and hojicha-runtime 0.2.2.

name: osteak
summary: The Elm Architecture for ratatui, with a built-in runner or your own event loop.
notes: update(&mut self, msg) returns a Cmd<Msg> holding an Action (None, Quit, Task for a future, Batch) and a dirty flag; the runtime or your own loop runs the Action and feeds the result back as a message.

subscriptions(&self) returns Vec<Sub<Msg>>, each an id plus a Stream; the built-in runner starts, keeps and cancels streams by id (https://github.com/os-tack/osteak/blob/main/src/sub.rs). With your own event loop you manage the streams yourself.
view(&mut self, frame: &mut Frame) draws into a ratatui Frame; it takes &mut self for ratatui stateful widgets.
Cmd::map lets a parent compose a child model (see the multi_pane example).

name: teatui
summary: An experimental Elm-like layer over ratatui that keeps mutation to a minimum.
notes: update is fn(Model, Msg) -> Update<Model, Effect>, with Update::Next(model, Option<Effect>) or Update::Exit; an Effect is your own enum, and the effects function you pass to teatui::start runs it (async with the tokio feature) and returns an Option<Msg>.

No subscription function: terminal events are the only source, read by the runtime and converted through Msg: From<crossterm::event::Event>; any other long-running source is an Effect that update re-issues.
view is fn(Model) -> Widget, a ratatui widget.
Moved from GitHub to Codeberg in 2026; the GitHub repository is archived.

name: Bubble Tea
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal apps in Go, with the largest TUI ecosystem around it.
notes: No subscriptions function: a subscription is a Cmd that blocks on a channel or reschedules itself.
Program.Send feeds messages from outside the program.
Bubbles (components), Lip Gloss (styling) and Huh (forms) are built on it; v2 moved to charm.land/bubbletea/v2.

name: The Composable Architecture
summary: State, actions and reducers that return effects, for SwiftUI and UIKit apps, with composition and exhaustive testing.
notes: Reducers return Effect values; long-running effects with cancellation stand in for subscriptions.
Superset: child features with their own state, actions and reducer compose into a parent, and TestStore checks every state change and every effect a test causes.
Dependencies are injected and replaced in tests.

name: Mobius.swift
summary: The Swift port of Mobius by Spotify: a TEA loop that feeds any view layer.
notes: Headless: there is no view function; the loop drives UIKit or SwiftUI through a connection.

name: Mobius
summary: The Spotify framework for state and side effects, used in its Android apps.
notes: update returns the next model with effects, which effect handlers run.
An EventSource feeds events from outside the loop.
Headless: the view is any Android UI connected to the loop.

name: Mobius.kt
summary: Mobius for Kotlin Multiplatform: update functions in common Kotlin, run on every target.

name: Elmslie
summary: TEA for Kotlin with first-class Android support, by Vivid Money.
notes: Modular: core, Android lifecycle, RxJava and Jetpack Compose artifacts.

name: Tea-bag
summary: A TEA implementation for Kotlin built on coroutines.

name: Dartea
summary: An MVU engine for Flutter inspired by TEA and Elmish.

name: mvu_layer
summary: Elm-inspired state management for Flutter: update is the only place that changes the model.

name: mvu_flutter
summary: A fuller Elm-style implementation for Flutter, with detailed docs.

name: Milo
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal apps in Python, with commands, sagas and subscriptions (ticks, terminal resize).
notes: To check: whether commands are returned from the reducer or started beside it (a saga runner would make it TEA-adjacent).

name: Joy
summary: A framework for building web apps in Roc with the Elm shape, compiled to WebAssembly.
notes: update returns (Model, List(Effect(Msg))): effects are data that the host runs.
subscriptions is a function of the model (Model -> List(Sub(Msg))): a source stops when it leaves the list.
Only the browser side exists so far; the full-stack part (server functions) is a stated goal, not shipped.

name: LeanTEA
summary: A small full-stack framework in Lean 4 whose terminal runtime is a Model, Msg, update, Cmd and Sub loop.
notes: The terminal runtime has update : Msg -> Model -> Model x Cmd Msg, where a Cmd is a list of IO actions that yield messages.
subs is a function of the model (Model -> Sub Msg), but the terminal runtime only polls stdin; tick sources are declared and not run there.
The web side (WebApp) is a stateless server step, Msg -> Model -> Model, with the model carried in a request header and no Cmd.

name: Skald
summary: An Elm-architecture GUI framework for Odin that rebuilds the view every frame on a Vulkan renderer.
notes: update :: proc(s: State, m: Msg) -> (State, skald.Command(Msg)); a Command covers delays, file IO, dialogs, windows and worker threads.
No subscriptions function: a recurring timer is a cmd_delay that update reschedules on every Tick, and the App has hooks such as on_key and on_system_theme_change.

name: ZigZag
summary: A Bubble Tea style TUI framework for Zig with typed Model, update and view and over 40 components.
notes: update(self: *Model, msg, ctx) returns a Cmd(Msg) union; the model is changed in place.
No subscriptions function: Cmd.every and Cmd.tick ask the runtime for repeating or one-shot Tick messages, and AsyncRunner delivers the results of background tasks.

name: Fern
summary: A TUI framework for Zig with an init, update, view loop, spring animation and a mouse zone manager.
notes: update(state, msg, alloc) returns ?Cmd(Msg); a Cmd is none, quit, batch, sequence, task (worker thread), after or every.
No subscriptions function: an every Cmd fires once and update returns another one to keep ticking.
Beta, and Zig 0.16 only.

name: Sky
summary: An Elm-syntax language that compiles to Go, where init, update, view and subscriptions run as a server-driven web app, a wasm client, a terminal UI or a native app.
notes: update : Msg -> Model -> ( Model, Cmd Msg ), with an extra Db argument first in the server-driven Sky.Live shape; effects are typed Tasks run through Cmd.perform.
subscriptions : Model -> Sub Msg, for example Time.every; on Sky.Live a subscription is pushed to the page over SSE.
Not Elm and not built on its runtime: the compiler is a Rust binary that emits Go. Any Go package is reachable through typed bindings (sky add), in place of ports.
Superset: server-side TEA in the Sky.Live shape, and the same program built as a wasm client, a terminal UI or a native app.

name: Abies
summary: Model-View-Update for .NET that renders the same program as static HTML, over a server WebSocket, in WebAssembly or on WinUI 3 controls.
notes: Transition(model, message) returns a (Model, Command) tuple; Command is an open interface of records that an interpreter runs, and results come back as messages.
Subscriptions(model) returns a Subscription value (Every, Batch, or a keyed Create source); the runtime starts and stops sources as the value changes.
Superset: four render modes (static, server, WASM, auto) and a native WinUI 3 renderer share one core, and only View differs.

name: Rooibos
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal apps in Ruby, built on RatatuiRuby.
notes: Update is a lambda (message, model) that returns the new model, or [model, command]; commands such as Command.wait, Command.http and Command.batch are values the runtime runs in the background.
No subscriptions function: a timer is a Command.tick that Update re-issues, and Command::Custom is a long-running command with a cancellation token that sends messages with out.put.
In beta: the docs of the guides are partly stubs, so the grades come from the source and the command docs.

name: re-alm
summary: An Elm Architecture experiment in ClojureScript, rendered with Reagent.
notes: Update takes (model, msg) and returns the new model, or a model with effects attached by with-fx; effects are records that the runtime executes.
The optional subscriptions function takes the model and returns topics such as time/every and websocket; the runtime diffs them after every update.
Messages are keywords or tagged vectors, matched with core.match by convention. The last push was in January 2018.

name: Mosaic
summary: A terminal UI framework for OCaml that implements the Elm Architecture, with CSS Flexbox and Grid layout.
notes: update : msg -> model -> model * msg Cmd.t, with Cmd.perform, Cmd.exec and Cmd.batch as values.
subscriptions : model -> msg Sub.t declares keys, mouse, timers (Sub.every, Sub.after) and workers; a timer or worker lives as long as its id stays declared.

name: Meltea
summary: The Elm Architecture for OCaml and Melange, with views written in mlx and compiled to DOM templates like Svelte, no virtual DOM.
notes: Program.element takes update : msg -> model -> model * msg Cmd.t and subscriptions : model -> msg Sub.t; Program.sandbox is the form with a plain update and no Cmd or Sub (the README example uses it).
Cmd (none, batch, perform, focus, port) and Sub (every, hash) are values that Program runs; Cmd.port only sends a value out to JavaScript.
Superset: server rendering and hydration build the same module for the browser and for a native or Node server.
Runs on native OCaml and compiles to JavaScript with Melange.

name: Oak
summary: An Elm-style frontend framework for PureScript, with routing, storage and navigation commands built in.
notes: Update is split in two pure functions: update :: Msg -> Model -> Model, then next :: Msg -> Model -> Cmd Msg, which receives the new model and returns the command; both are pure.
subscriptions :: Model -> Array (Subscription Msg) is re-run after every update and reconciled (onInterval, onTimeout, onOnline, window events); the message type needs an Eq instance for that.

name: Scalafui
summary: An experimental Elm Architecture for Scala.js, with Cats Effect commands and React rendering.
notes: update(msg, model): (Model, Cmd[Msg]); a Cmd is a lazy Cats Effect IO that the runtime runs and turns into a message.
subscriptions: Model => Sub[Msg] (Sub.every, Sub.timeout, Sub.fromEvent, fs2 streams); the runtime compares ids after each update to start and stop streams, and Sub.fromResource adapts callback APIs.
Superset: Feature, slots and bindings compose stateful parts with outputs, on top of the plain Program.

name: SageTUI
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal apps in F#, run with App.run and a flexbox layout.
notes: A program is a record of Init, Update, View and Subscribe: update is msg -> model -> model * Cmd, and Subscribe is model -> Sub list (keys, timers, mouse, resize, custom sources).
The runtime starts and stops timer and custom subscriptions by id after each update.
Cmd covers async tasks, delays and quit; a test harness can advance time for delayed Cmd chains.

name: ReactiveElmish.Avalonia
summary: Elmish stores for Avalonia: an Elmish loop per view model, with the view in static Avalonia XAML.
notes: Built on the Elmish library (v4): mkAvaloniaProgram takes init and update returning Model * Cmd, and Program.withSubscription takes a keyed function of the model.
The view is static XAML bound to view model properties (Bind projects the model), not a function that returns a view tree; graded like Elmish.WPF.
A store can be local to a view model or shared as a global app store; subscriptions of a view model end with mkStoreWithTerminate.

name: MVUish.Avalonia
summary: MVU for Avalonia in F# and C#, where the view builds real controls once and binds them to a stream of models.
notes: The view runs once with an IObservable of the model and binds properties directly, with no view tree and no diffing; the README itself says it is not strict Elm, where the view is a pure function of the model.
Update returns the new model and a command (a function that receives dispatch); subscriptions follow Elmish v4: a keyed list that is a function of the model, started and stopped by the runtime.
The F# API and a C# module (Command, Subscription) share one runtime.

name: Oolong
summary: MVU for Kotlin Multiplatform: update returns the new model and an effect, and each platform supplies a render function.
notes: Update is (Msg, Model) -> Pair of Model and Effect; an Effect is a suspend function that receives dispatch, launched in a new coroutine by the runtime (none and batch combine them).
No subscription function and the docs do not mention one: a long-running source is an Effect that loops or collects a flow, and the runtime job cancels it on dispose (graded from runtime.kt).
The view returns Props that a platform render function draws; the last release is from 2022.

name: Keemun
summary: The Elm Architecture for shared Kotlin and SwiftUI code, with effects as plain values run by an EffectHandler.
notes: Update takes a message and the state and returns the new state with a set of Effect values; an EffectHandler runs each effect in its own coroutine (Swift: a Combine publisher or an async task) and dispatches messages back.
No subscription function: a long-running source is an effect that keeps dispatching, or a publisher in Swift, cancelled when the store goes away (graded from the source).
The Swift version lives in pavelannin/Keemun-Swift; a StateTransform maps the state to a ViewState that Compose or SwiftUI draws.

name: Puer
summary: TEA for Dart and Flutter: a pure update returns the new state and a list of effect values for handlers to run.
notes: Update is (State, Message) -> Next of an optional new state and a list of Effect values; an EffectHandler performs them and calls emit to send messages back.

No subscription function: a handler keeps emit and sends later, and StreamEffectHandler in puer_effect_handlers starts and stops a stream on start and end effects (that package is in the repository, not yet on pub.dev).
The core is pure Dart and puer_flutter adds the FeatureBuilder widgets; time-travel debugging is included.

name: TermUI
summary: A terminal runtime for Elixir on the Elm architecture, where view returns one Frame.
notes: Update returns the new state or a tuple of state and a list of command values (message, send, timer, async, clipboard, shutdown).
No subscription function: a Command.timer fires once, so a repeating source reschedules it from update, and an optional handle_info callback turns BEAM process messages into state and commands.
The release is 2.0.0-rc.1; the repository moved from pcharbon70 to agentjido.

name: effect-tea
summary: The Elm Architecture on Effect v4 for any renderer, with commands and subscriptions as data and parent and child composition declared in the program.
notes: update is curried, (message) => (state) => { state, commands?, events? }, and may return reject to ignore a message; commands are plain data that runCommand turns into an Effect, and subscriptions(state) returns a HashMap of keyed Effect Channels that the runtime starts and stops.
The library ships no renderer: run hands a stream of frames ({ model, dispatch }) to a bridge, with small snabbdom and React bridges in the examples; the model is made from the state by makeModel.
Superset: parent and child composition (children, events, external messages) and the testing tools (rehearse, simulate, dispatchViolations).

name: Hypertea
summary: A tiny TypeScript TEA runtime for the client side of server-rendered apps, from one island to a single-page application.
notes: update is (model, message) => [model, effects], with effects as data run by a runEffect adapter that gets an abort signal; an effectless program omits it.
subscriptions(model) returns an array of keyed subscriptions (every, keyPressed, windowResized, and a live SSE one), matched by slot and key after each update.
mountProgram and start return a handle with dispatch() and call() for messages from outside; an ESLint purity config bans unmanaged effects in update.

name: tea-set
summary: Elm-style Cmd, Sub, Task, Result and RemoteData for TypeScript, with a small runtime that drives the init, update, subscriptions and view loop.
notes: update(msg, model) returns [Model, Cmd<Msg>]; a Cmd is data (none, batch, map, effect) and nothing runs until the runtime performs it, with Task for promise work that is aborted on stop().
subscriptions(model) returns a Sub, and the runtime starts, restarts and stops its sources by key and params after each update.
view is a callback you supply, so any renderer works; element() returns { dispatch, stop }, an incoming port for outside code.

name: @oakoliver/bubbletea
summary: An unaffiliated TypeScript port of Bubble Tea for Node.js and Bun, at parity with Bubble Tea v2.1.1.
notes: A Model class has init(): Cmd, update(msg): [Model, Cmd] and view(); a Cmd is a function, as in Bubble Tea.
No subscriptions function, graded like Bubble Tea: a subscription is a Cmd that reschedules itself (Tick, Every).
Program.send feeds messages from outside; the port has its own sibling ports of Bubbles, Lip Gloss and others.

name: bare-tui
summary: A small TUI framework for the Bare runtime, shaped after Bubble Tea, with its own components and styling helper.
notes: update(msg) returns [model, command] (a bare model means no command); messages are plain objects tagged by type, and mutating this is the idiomatic style.
A Cmd is a function returning a Msg or a Promise of one; there is no subscriptions function, so a subscription is a Cmd that reschedules itself (tick, every). Graded like Bubble Tea.
Program.send feeds messages from outside the loop; experimental, before version 1.0.

name: Cinnamon Bun
summary: A TypeScript port of Bubble Tea for Bun, with the model as plain functions init, update and view.
notes: update(model, msg) returns [Model, Cmd]; a Cmd is a function, and messages are objects tagged by type.
No subscriptions function, graded like Bubble Tea: a subscription is a Cmd that reschedules itself (Tick, Every).
Program.Send feeds messages from outside; components come from the separate Cinnamon library.

name: Caibao
summary: A Bubble Tea inspired TUI framework for Bun, with components and a Lip Gloss style styling system.
notes: A Model class has init(): Cmd, update(msg): [Model, Cmd] and view(); a Cmd is a function returning a Msg or a Promise of one.
No subscriptions function, graded like Bubble Tea: a subscription is a Cmd that reschedules itself (Tick, Every).
The runtime handle has send(msg) for messages from outside; an independent implementation, not a port of the Go code.

name: masc
summary: Bubble Tea models with Vecty views: The Elm Architecture for browser apps in Go, compiled to WebAssembly.
notes: Init() Cmd and Update(Msg) (Model, Cmd) as in Bubble Tea; Render(send) returns HTML components and sends messages with the send function it is given. A model is a stateful pointer that mutates itself.
No subscriptions function: Every and Tick are Cmds that reschedule, graded like Bubble Tea.
Program.Send feeds messages from outside; renders are scheduled on animation frames.

name: Phoenix
summary: A modular TUI framework for Go with a Bubble Tea style Elm Architecture package, its own components, styling and layout.
notes: Init() Cmd, Update(Msg) (Model, Cmd) and View() string with a generic Program; a Cmd is func() Msg, as in Bubble Tea.
No subscriptions function: Tick sleeps then returns a message, so a subscription is a Cmd that reschedules itself. Graded like Bubble Tea.
Program.Send feeds messages from other goroutines; the repo is a monorepo of ten libraries.

name: Boba
summary: A Bubble Tea inspired TUI framework on ratatui, with declarative subscriptions the runtime diffs on every cycle.
notes: update takes &mut self and returns a Command<Msg> (none, message, perform for futures, batch, sequence, quit); the view draws into a ratatui Frame.
subscriptions() returns a Vec<Subscription<Msg>> from the model; the runtime diffs them by id on every cycle, starting new ones and aborting removed ones.
A Component trait nests sub-models with their own message type, mapped with Command::map; 18 ready-made widgets.

name: teapot
summary: A Bubble Tea inspired TUI framework with forms, components and styling, where the view returns a string.
notes: update takes &mut self and returns an Option<Cmd<Msg>> (quit, perform, perform_async, tick, run_process, batch, sequence).
No subscription function: Cmd::tick is a one-shot timer that update re-issues, and terminal events reach the model through handle_event, which maps an Event to a message.
The README says it is under active development and not production-ready.

name: A3S TUI
summary: A TUI framework with an Elm style update loop, a virtual DOM like Element tree and flexbox layout, aimed at AI agent interfaces.
notes: ElementModel has fn update(&mut self, msg) -> Option<Cmd<Msg>> and fn view(&self) -> Element<Msg>; an older string view model exists beside it.
No subscription function: cmd::tick is a one-shot delay that update re-issues (the chat example reschedules its stream and spinner ticks this way).
Cmd is an async future (msg, batch, sequence, tick, perform, quit).

name: Rustea
summary: A small Rust port of the go-tea library: update returns an optional boxed command and messages are downcast from Any.
notes: update takes &mut self and a Box<dyn Any> message and returns an Option<Command>; a Command is a boxed closure returning an Option<Message>, run on its own thread, so it may block.
No subscription function: key, mouse and resize events arrive as messages, and a long-running source is a command that blocks or that update re-issues.
The repository is a restored copy of the lazops/rustea crate code; last commit in April 2025.

name: Limoni
summary: A Go terminal UI engine with an allocation-free renderer, an immediate mode beside an Elm architecture program, and a semantic tree that tests and AI agents drive.
notes: The Model interface of core/engine is Init() []Cmd, Update(Msg) UpdateResult and View(*terminal.Frame); update changes the model through a pointer receiver and returns an UpdateResult of Commands, Redraw and Quit.
Cmd is func(context.Context) Msg, a cancellable command the runtime runs on a worker goroutine, its result sent back to Update (NowCmd, ExecCmd, NotifyCmd, SuspendCmd).

No subscription function: key, mouse and resize events arrive as messages (KeyPressMsg), and a timer or stream is a command that update re-issues; pending results are dropped when the context is cancelled.
The same library also has an immediate mode (limoni.Run) with no messages, and compat/bubbletea runs Bubble Tea models on it.

name: Actomaton
summary: An actor-based state machine for Swift async/await, inspired by Elm and TCA: reducers return Effect values, with effect queues for cancellation and SwiftUI and UIKit stores.
notes: Reducer { action, state, environment in ... } changes an inout State and returns an Effect<Action> (Effect.empty, next, fireAndForget, init with an async closure, sequence, stream, cancel), which the Actomaton actor runs.

No subscription function: Effect.sequence(id:) turns an AsyncSequence into actions and Effect.stream(id:) bridges delegates and callbacks, both long-running and stopped with Effect.cancel(id:) or by an EffectQueue policy.
Views: ActomatonUI has a Store for SwiftUI and UIKit; a SwiftUI view reads the state through WithViewStore and sends actions with send.

Superset: reducers of child features compose into a parent with Reducer.combine and contramap over CasePath and KeyPath, EffectQueue policies (runNewest, runOldest with suspendNew or discardNew, delays) cancel or suspend effects, and TestActomaton checks every state change and received action.

name: WebSharper.Mvu
summary: Elm-inspired Model-View-Update for WebSharper client apps, where the render function is called once with a reactive View of the model.
notes: App.Create takes update : Message -> Model -> Action<Message, Model>; Action is DoNothing, SetModel, UpdateModel, Command of (Dispatch -> unit), CommandAsync of (Dispatch -> Async<unit>) or CombinedAction, and the runtime applies it (DispatchAsync wraps an async call whose result becomes a message).
The render function takes Dispatch and a WebSharper.UI View<Model> and is called once; the reactive View, not a new render, follows each change of the model.
No subscription function: a long-running source is a Command or CommandAsync that holds dispatch, or one update re-issues; App.WithInitAction runs one at start.
Paging (App.CreatePaged), routing bound to the model (App.WithRouting), local storage of the model and RemoteDev time travel debugging; WebSharper JavaScript interop is called from inside commands.

name: Raxol
summary: An Elixir runtime where one Elm architecture module, run as an OTP GenServer, renders to a terminal, a Phoenix LiveView page, an SSH session and MCP tools for agents.
notes: The behaviour Raxol.Core.Runtime.Application has init(context), update(message, model) returning {model, [command]} and view(model); the docs say commands are executed by the runtime, keeping update pure.
Commands are Raxol.Core.Runtime.Directive values (stop, schedule, spawn_task), run by Directive.Executor; a scheduled payload or the result of a task comes back to update as a message.

subscribe(model) returns a list of Subscription values (interval, events, file_watch, custom); after each update the Dispatcher calls it again (sync_subscriptions) and stops the removed ones and starts the new ones.
No ports: an optional handle_message(message, model) callback turns other BEAM process messages into a model and commands.

Superset: the same module renders to four surfaces (a termbox2 terminal, Phoenix LiveView, Erlang SSH and MCP tools), with OTP crash isolation per component, hot code reload and agent packages beside it.

name: Xelmish
summary: Elmish for 2D games: an XNA game loop on MonoGame, where view returns a list of viewables that draw to a SpriteBatch and read input each frame.
notes: Xelmish.Program.runGameLoop takes a standard Elmish Program<_, _, _, Viewable list>, swaps in its own setState with Program.withSetState and calls Program.run, so the Elmish runtime runs Cmd and the keyed subscriptions of Program.withSubscription (the sub-model sample uses one for a timer).

view model dispatch returns Viewable values (colour, image, text, and the OnUpdate helpers whilekeydown, onkeydown, onclick) that the MonoGame loop runs each frame; input dispatches messages from them.
Updated in 2025 to Elmish 5 and MonoGame 3.8.4.

name: tview (ayn2op)
summary: A declarative Go terminal UI framework inspired by Elm, where a value model returns itself and a command from Update and builds a widget tree in View; used by the Discord client discordo.
notes: The interface Model[M] has Init() Cmd, Update(Msg) (M, Cmd) and View() Widget; the docs ask for value receivers and an immutable model, which only Update changes by returning it.

Msg is any (a type switch in Update); key, mouse, resize, paste and clipboard events arrive as KeyMsg, MouseMsg, ResizeMsg and the like, and Widget.Handle turns input in its area into a message (button OnClick, Map like Html.map).

Cmd is a closed set of values the Application runs (Task, Batch, Quit, Suspend, SetTitle, Notify, SetClipboard, GetClipboard, RequestTerminalInfo, WriteRaw); a Task (func() Msg) runs on its own goroutine and its message is queued back to Update.
No subscription function: a timer or a stream is a Task that Update issues again, and terminal events come in as messages.

name: Swiftea
summary: A small TEA loop for Swift on Combine, under 200 lines: a reducer returns the next state and commands, a command handler turns each command into a publisher of events, and outdated commands can be cancelled.
notes: Reducer<State, Event, Command> wraps a closure (State, Event) -> Next<State, Command>; Next is empty, next(State), dispatch([Command]), nextAndDispatch, or the Cancellable forms that also list the commands that cancel this one.

Commands are values of an Equatable enum; CommandHandler<Command, Event, Environment> maps each to an AnyPublisher<Event, Never>, and the Store feeds every event the publisher emits back to the reducer.
No subscription function: a long-running source is a command whose publisher keeps emitting events, stopped when a later command in its cancellable list arrives.
Headless: there is no view function; a ViewStore maps the state to a UI state through stateMapper and view events to events through eventMapper, and UIKit subscribes to its statePublisher.
No ports: the Environment of the command handler holds the repositories and the module output that talk to the rest of the app.

name: FSharp.Windows.Dsl
summary: A native F# DSL for WPF on Elmish: view returns a virtual tree that a reconciler diffs into the live WPF elements, with no XAML, no MVVM and no INotifyPropertyChanged.
notes: Program.runWindow takes a standard Elmish Program<unit, 'model, 'msg, VirtualNode> (Elmish.Program.mkProgram init update view), adds Program.withSetState for the reconciler and runs it with Program.runWithDispatch, which marshals each dispatch to the WPF UI thread; the Elmish 5 runtime runs Cmd and the keyed subscriptions of Program.withSubscription.
view model dispatch returns a VirtualNode tree of generated control wrappers (window, stackPanel, button with Button.onClick); Dsl.update diffs it into the live element tree.

Program.runChildWindow and runDialogWindow open windows with loops of their own; FSharp.Windows.Dsl.Elmish adds keyed cancellable task commands (Cmd.OfTask.runKeyed, Cmd.cancel) scoped to a window, and an AppBus for publish and subscribe between windows.

name: Oak (Monad)
summary: The web stack of the Monad language: an Elm-shaped app compiled to wasm, with a pure update that returns Command values and subscriptions declared from the model.
notes: update : Model -> Msg -> Pair Model (Command Unit Msg); Command is none, quit, dispatch, perform, after, focus, after_render or batch, and the runtime runs it.
Program.with_subs takes subs : Model -> List (Subscription Msg) (window and document events, animation frames), registered by the runtime from the model.
Command.perform hands an effect value to a Host that the app writes, in place of ports; the oak mote also renders pages on the server (Ssr) for the http mote.
